answer: In the NLS processed sample (n = 8,773), an unadjusted binomial-logit regression of BA DEGREE COMPLETED on SAMPLE_RACE with White as the reference category produces a coefficient on the Hispanic indicator of -0.9241 (Wald 95 % CI [-1.3997, -0.4485]; z = -3.81; p = 0.00014). This is the race-dummy coefficient closest to the target factor of -0.9568 cited in the question (|Δ| = 0.033). The corresponding ordered pair is **Hispanic versus White**, indicating that Hispanic respondents in this dataset have lower log-odds of completing a BA than White respondents. Equivalently, exp(-0.9241) ≈ 0.397, so Hispanic respondents' estimated odds of BA completion are roughly 60 % lower than those of White respondents in this sample.

payload.hypothesis: In an unadjusted logistic regression of BA-degree completion on race with White as the reference category (n = 8,773; White n=5,337 with k=189 BA completers; Black n=2,113 with k=28; Hispanic n=1,323 with k=19), the coefficient on the Hispanic indicator is -0.9241 (Wald 95% CI [-1.400, -0.449], z = -3.81, p = 0.00014). This is the race-dummy coefficient closest to the stated factor of -0.9568, so the pair whose factor of BA completion is -0.9568 (when compared to the other) is Hispanic vs White -- Hispanic respondents in this dataset have lower log-odds, and roughly 60% lower odds, of BA completion than White respondents. (The Black-vs-White coefficient is -1.0057, |Δ|=0.049, also within the 0.05 tie-band but the more distant match; the fully-adjusted model flips both race coefficients positive, confirming -0.9568 is the headline unadjusted race-only logit coefficient on Hispanic.)
payload.workflow: Loaded data/nls_ses_processed.csv (8773 x 9, 0 NaN). Verified SAMPLE_RACE levels {White:5337, Black:2113, Hispanic:1323} and BA DEGREE COMPLETED {False:8537, True:236}. Computed crude completion rates p_White=0.03541, p_Black=0.01325, p_Hispanic=0.01436 and crude log-ORs with White reference (-1.0057 Black, -0.9241 Hispanic). Fit (1) unadjusted and (2) fully-adjusted binomial logit GLMs via statsmodels (White reference). Confirmed via sensitivity sweep (14 model variants: sex only, SES only, family-size only, ability only, percentile only, full adj, full adj + FS^2, raw vs z-continuous controls, single-race dummies, HC1 robust SE) that unadjusted race-only is the sole model with any race coefficient within 0.05 of -0.9568. Applied the directive's tiebreaker: distance to target wins -> Hispanic vs White (|Δ|=0.033 vs 0.049).
